rules_evaluated.evidence: L5-6: 'Trust isn't watching harder. It's verification you can run without being there.' Doc Mood arc places M3 at 'earned trust'; M3-in-detail: 'The discipline is installed before M4's first unwatched send-off, so nobody feels exposed when the long run finally happens' and 'What M3 refuses: frame Q+S as compliance (they're infrastructure).' The Big Idea's reframe away from surveillance toward runnable verification is the same move the doc describes — trust as infrastructure you built, not vigilance you perform. No drift.

One-sentence state: the student leaves having earned two sign-offs (staff engineer on the test-strategy skill, CISO on the STRIDE/ADR decision) rather than having survived a compliance check, and that earned-not-watched trust is what lets M4 send a session off unwatched without anyone feeling exposed. L106-109 'Next': 'Two signatures, earned... Module 4 turns the discipline inward' matches doc's 'earned trust' and its own M4-bridge line verbatim in spirit. Mood is honoured, not resolved early — M4 still owns the actual send-off experience; this file only installs the discipline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea leads with 'verification,' not a failure word. All section headers (Earn the trust / Sharpen the skill from evidence / Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye / Clear the session / Key Concepts / Optional challenges / Bring to Module 4 / Next) are discipline- or action-named. 'STRIDE' (L39) and 'the lethal trifecta' (L16) read failure-shaped but are named canonical results (Kohnfelder & Garg 1999 memo; Willison's trifecta) — exactly the carve-out's own worked example.

Two claims in this file contradict a cross-exercise design bet the strategy doc states explicitly, and both are independently confirmed against the sibling exercise files themselves (not just the doc). (1) L23 WYL bullet: 'Invoke curated access-control-analysis and STRIDE skills on a feature you're shipping (each as a subagent, fresh context)'. Doc M3-in-detail: 'Subagents introduced, deliberately — and only once. The STRIDE pass is the dispatch... The access-surface pass invokes its skill in-thread... That three-way contrast is half the pedagogy: the student leaves M3 knowing which jobs belong in which thread, not merely that subagents exist.' Confirmed current in the actual exercise: curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md maintainer block, dated 2026-09-04: 'This exercise invokes its skill in-thread, and that is the design... Do not add a dispatch clause here to match the module's subagent theme.' 'Each as a subagent' misstates the design the doc calls half the pedagogy. (2) L26 WYL bullet ('invoke it on the security-tested feature') plus maintainer Push-back-moves L152 and Per-phase-failure-mode table L196 (both: 'run the skill on the feature you just security-tested'). Doc M3-in-detail: 'Invocation closes the loop, and it runs on the whole codebase in the quality-side worktree rather than on the security-tested feature: the skill is a claim about how testing works here, so the honest test of it is the repo, not one feature.' Confirmed in the actual exercise: curriculum/exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md L34 header 'Phase 2: Invoke the skill on this codebase', L39 'this worktree holds the full codebase. Invoke it on the code as it stands in front of you.' Harm present, not hypothetical: `pre-cohort-todos.md` already logs the identical 'security-tested feature' phrase as inaccurate in the `ae101-m3-sharpen-skill` prompt fence and left it unchanged only because a fresh session recovers by grounding on the ADR — that accept-note covers the PROMPT fence, not this file's own WYL bullet or its two trainer-script tables (Push-back-moves, Decision-points), which a trainer reads directly and would use to coach students toward the wrong invocation target on both counts (wrong thread for access-control-analysis, wrong scope for the test-strategy invocation).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: L23: scope 'each as a subagent' to STRIDE only — access-control-analysis runs in-thread per map-the-access-surface.md's own maintainer note. L26, L152, L196: replace 'invoke...on the security-tested feature' with 'invoke...on this codebase' (the quality-side worktree), matching author-test-strategy-skill.md Phase 2 and the doc's stated reasoning.
